post.caption: Prehnite grows in clusters like grapes. The rounded clusters form in cavities of volcanic rock. Its color is pale green, sometimes with a yellowish tint. It is nicknamed Cape emerald, though it is not an emerald. The name honors Colonel von Prehn, and dates to the late 1700s. Prehnite measures 6 to 6.5 on the Mohs hardness scale. It is usually cut as a smooth cabochon or as beads. Some prehnite from Australia is cut with facets too. Cat's eye prehnite has been reported, and it is very rare. Rare orange crystals have turned up in South Africa's Kalahari manganese field.
